subject: botany
question_text: What is growth? What is the difference between growth in living organisms and growth in non-living objects?

verification.note: Chapter 1 (The Living World) is sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Botany Fastrack, book p.3 (VSAQ 6 of 9), which prints the question and a model answer but no star ranks and no year citations. Only one source book is held for botany — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand is physics-only and no botany board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the board-paper back-test are both structurally impossible for this chapter; 'not checked' here means exactly that, never 'checked and clean'. The 1+1 mark split is a claim until a TS IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. The book words the contrast as 'internal'/'external' growth; the card uses the standard terms intrinsic/extrinsic with the same meaning.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Definition of growth
lines: Growth is an irreversible increase in the size,
dry weight and number of cells of an organism.

lines.text: Growth = irreversible increase in size and mass

steps.why: 'Irreversible' is the load-bearing word — a temporary swelling caused by taking up water can reverse, so it is not growth.
common_mistakes: Leaving out 'irreversible'. A reversible increase (swelling) is not growth.
Writing only 'increase in size'. Add dry weight or number of cells to show real body material increased.
steps.memory_tip: Growth is the increase that stays: irreversible increase in size, dry weight, cell number.
steps.margin_note: The definition earns this mark; keep it to one sentence.

steps.label: Living vs non-living growth
lines: In living organisms growth is intrinsic —
it takes place from inside the body by
In non-living objects growth is extrinsic —
material only accumulates on the outer
surface. Example: a sand mound grows.
steps.why: The same word 'growth' covers two different processes: living bodies add material from inside by cell division; non-living objects only collect material on the outside. The book words this as internal versus external growth — intrinsic and extrinsic are the standard terms with the same meaning.
common_mistakes: Writing 'living things grow, non-living things do not'. Non-living objects can grow — but only by surface accumulation.
Swapping the terms. Intrinsic = from inside = living; extrinsic = on the outside = non-living.
steps.memory_tip: IN-trinsic = from INside (living); EX-trinsic = on the EXterior (non-living).
steps.margin_note: Give both sides — one line for living, one for non-living.

insider_note: The word 'irreversible' and the inside-versus-surface contrast are the two things the examiner checks first.
